brief.symptoms: On 32-bit architectures, decoding a crafted Kafka response panics at runtime instead of returning a decode error. The process crashes with a slice length out of range, making it impossible to test or run the library on 32-bit platforms.
brief.evidence:
real_decoder_test.go:70: getArrayLength() gotLen = -2147483648, want -1
real_decoder_test.go:73: getArrayLength() gotErr = <nil>, want kafka: error decoding packet: invalid array length
hints: The decoder returns a nonsensical negative length and no error when it should reject an out-of-range value before allocating any memory.
Look at the array-length and buffer-sizing paths in real_decoder.go - the sign check that guards against invalid lengths is missing for at least one of those paths.

When the raw bytes encode a value that is valid as an unsigned 32-bit integer but wraps to a large negative number after a signed cast, the decoder does not detect the invalid length before passing it to make(). On a 64-bit host the value stays positive and the later bounds check catches it, but on a 32-bit host the cast produces a value that escapes all guards and reaches the allocator.
brief.lesson: Casting a uint32 to int32 then to int can wrap to a large negative number on 32-bit systems where int is 32 bits wide. The fix adds an explicit `if tmp < -1` check in getArrayLength() to reject any negative length other than the sentinel -1 (null array), and replaces signed intermediate variables with uint64 arithmetic in the flexible decoder paths so that overflow cannot produce a value that bypasses the remaining() bounds check.
